patch.value: Session-topic provenance has no descriptor keys on any harness, and effort/role are wired for only claude-code and codex, so most fleet history records harness and model but nothing about the work's shape

The extensible provenance schema (ADR pm-oskdmu, shipped via pm-itsjf0) supports arbitrary dimensions, but the built-in descriptor table in src/core/shared/author.ts declares effort only for claude-code (CLAUDE_EFFORT) and codex (CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT/CODEX_EFFORT), role only for codex (CODEX_SESSION_ROLE), and topic for none of the seven agent harnesses (claude-code, codex, pi, opencode, cursor, aider, gemini-cli). Maintainers explicitly want attribution that includes the session topic and thinking level without any agent typing an identity flag. Each harness that exposes a topic/subject or effort signal needs its env keys declared; harnesses that expose none get an explicit null-mapping note so the gap is a documented harness limitation rather than an undiscovered omission.

Every built-in agent descriptor either declares keys for topic, effort and role or carries a recorded no-signal note for the missing dimension; detection tests prove each declared key flows into history provenance; fleet attribution (pm-gw6uyq) can group recorded history by topic and effort for the harnesses that expose them; no agent is ever required to set PM_AUTHOR or an identity flag
Attribution rich enough that per-harness, per-model, per-effort and per-topic fleet analytics (pm-gw6uyq) run on recorded history alone

Maintainer directive: harness, model, thinking level and session topic must all be auto-detected; the schema shipped extensible but the built-in descriptor table only covers two harnesses for effort and one for role

value.text:
Re-measured 2026-07-28 over 40,353 entries: zero carry any session topic, session role, or task-shape descriptor. Searching every entry key across the corpus, the complete set is ts, author, op, patch, before_hash, after_hash, message, author_source, agent_harness, agent_instance, agent_provenance and context. There is no session_topic, no agent_role, and no session key of any kind.

What this item can now treat as settled rather than open:

- The effort dimension SHIPPED and works. agent_provenance.effort reads {value: "xhigh", source: "environment"} on this session's entries, resolved from CLAUDE_EFFORT. So the claim that effort is wired for only two harnesses should be re-checked against the new agent_provenance shape rather than the old three-key descriptor, and the schema-extensibility objection is answered - a fourth dimension was added and populates.
- Sub-agent lineage signals ARE present in the environment and unused: CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 are both set alongside CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so a parent-child agent relationship is observable today and is recorded nowhere.
- Session TOPIC and ROLE remain the genuinely hard half, and the environment confirms why: nothing in the harness environment describes what the session is FOR. The full claude-code key set is CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_PID. Topic and role are therefore not detectable in principle from this signal source and must be SUPPLIED, which is consistent with the disposition already recorded elsewhere that role has no signal source anywhere.

The useful reframing for this item: three of the four dimensions it asks for split cleanly by source. Harness and instance and effort are DETECTED and now work. Model is absent from the environment entirely and needs a non-environment source. Topic and role are semantic and can only be supplied by the caller or inferred from the work itself, for example from the items an agent touches during a session, which is the one option that keeps the automatic-identity mandate intact.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Live provenance shape re-measured 2026-07-30 (evening), on a mutation written by this pass with no identity flag and no author environment variable set, which is the mandated mode.

The entry records author harness colon claude-code with author_source detected, agent_harness claude-code, agent_instance as an opaque identifier, and agent_provenance carrying two dimensions: model null, and effort with value xhigh and source environment. There is no session topic field, no session role field, and no harness version field anywhere on the entry. The full key set is after_hash, agent_harness, agent_instance, agent_provenance, author, author_source, before_hash, op, patch, ts.

So the state this item describes is unchanged and confirmed at HEAD: effort resolves and is correctly attributed to its source, which proves the provenance container is extensible in practice, and topic and role have no descriptor keys on any harness so they remain inexpressible rather than merely unpopulated. The model dimension is a separate problem with a separate owner, because the primary harness publishes no model key at all, so no additional key list can fix it.

One design consequence worth recording while the container is being extended. Topic and role differ from effort in kind: effort is published by the harness as an environment value, while a session topic or role is a description of intent that no harness publishes anywhere. If a dimension has no signal source, it must be supplied rather than detected, and the automatic-identity mandate says an agent should not have to type it. The only reconciliation is a session-scoped declaration made once, not per call: a value set on a focus or session record that every subsequent mutation in that session inherits automatically, recorded with a source naming the declaration rather than the environment. That keeps per-call invocations flag-free while making the dimension expressible, and it means the acceptance for topic and role should be a session-scope inheritance test rather than an environment-key test.

message: Record the session-scope inheritance design, since no harness publishes topic or role as an environment value

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Corpus measurement 2026-07-31 over all 44,408 history entries in this tracker, recorded here rather than as a new item because this issue already owns the topic/effort/role descriptor gap and its acceptance criteria already require the session-scoped declaration.

Coverage by dimension, counted from the raw streams: model appears on 2,814 entries and every one is an explicit null; effort appears on 471 entries, all of them observations, all attributed to claude-code, none earlier than 2026-07-27T12:46:06Z; role has never appeared on any entry from any harness. topic has never appeared, as this item states.

The codex asymmetry is now measured rather than inferred. codex declares effort via CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT and CODEX_EFFORT and role via CODEX_SESSION_ROLE, and across 3,223 codex-attributed entries neither dimension appears once. So for codex both declared extensible dimensions are inert on the real corpus, and claude-code is the only harness that has ever populated any dimension other than model.

Two structural findings were filed separately because they are defects in the recording mechanism rather than in the descriptor table, and either one alone would prevent this item's acceptance criteria from being verifiable. pm-9wbiye: resolveAgentProvenance writes an explicit null for the model dimension only, so once topic and role are declared their absence will be as unrecoverable as effort's is now. pm-1zhfls: the MCP server is spawned without CLAUDE_EFFORT and snapshots process.env at startup, so a session-scoped declaration inherited through the environment will not reach MCP-written entries at all - which matters directly for the second acceptance criterion here, since a declaration made once per session has to be honoured by every surface for the inheritance claim to hold.

Sequencing implication for this item: the explicit-unavailable generalization should land before new dimensions are declared, otherwise the descriptor work produces dimensions whose non-population cannot be distinguished from a legacy entry.
